subproblem.title: Foundations: Riesz representation of currents of locally finite mass with absolute continuity (REP), and calculus of integer multiplicity currents (IMC)
subproblem.statement: Two facts about currents in open subsets of ℝ^P (P, n ∈ ℕ arbitrary in each part), forming one conjunction. (REP) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) a current (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n) with M_W(T) < ∞ for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U. Then there are a Borel measure μ on ℝ^P and a map ξ from ℝ^P to n-vectors (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) such that: μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0; μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P; ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every x and every n-covector α, where |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm); T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); and, if in addition M_W(∂T) < ∞ for every such W (boundaryMassOn, read as 0 when n = 0), then μ(E) = 0 for every set E ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(E) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). (IMC) (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).

Source: Simon 6.2.7–2.8, 2.35–2.37 (REP; BV theorem 2.35 replaced by Lemma TD, step 8); 3.1.5(2), 3.1.6, 6.2.6, 6.2.9, 6.3.2(1) (IMC).
Part (REP).
Notation. 𝒟ⁿ(U):=TestFormOn U n; 𝕀:={increasing I=(i_1<⋯<i_n) in {1,…,P}}, e_I:=(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}), H:=EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝕀. For n-covectors α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_Iα(e_I)²)^{1/2} = ‖c(α)‖_H, where c(α):=(α(e_I))_{I∈𝕀} is a linear isomorphism onto H (injective: alternating forms are determined on increasing basis tuples; surjective: the alternating dx^I(v_1,…,v_n):=det((v_j)^{i_k})_{k,j} has dx^I(e_J)=δ_{IJ}); α=Σ_Iα(e_I)dx^I. If n>P, 𝕀=∅ and n-covectors vanish (n>P vectors are dependent). |ω|_∞:=sup_x|ω(x)|. n-vectors (MultiVector P n) are continuous linear functionals ζ on n-covectors, ⟨α,ζ⟩:=ζ(α).
(E1) If ω∈𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω⊆W, W open, W⊂⊂U, then |T(ω)|≤|ω|_∞M_W(T) (ω=0 if |ω|_∞=0, else ±ω/|ω|_∞ are admissible: massAdmissibleOn).
(E2) |β∧γ|≤|β||γ| (β a 1-, γ a k-covector) and |p_α^#γ|=|γ| (p_α : ℝ^P→ℝⁿ, x↦(x^{i_1},…,x^{i_n}), γ a k-covector on ℝⁿ): k!|γ|²=Σ_{i_1,…,i_k}γ(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_k})² (repeated indices vanish; each increasing tuple occurs k! times up to sign) is the basis-independent Hilbert–Schmidt norm of γ, so |·| is invariant under orthogonal coordinate changes; rotating to β=|β|e¹, β∧γ=|β|Σ_{I∌1}γ_Ie¹∧e^I has norm |β|(Σ_{I∌1}γ_I²)^{1/2}≤|β||γ|; p_α^# maps the orthonormal basis e^J of ℝⁿ to the orthonormal e^{α(J)}.
1. If n>P, test forms vanish, T=0, M_W(T)=0, and μ:=0, ξ:=0 satisfy all assertions. Let n≤P.
2. (Extension.) X:=U (open in ℝ^P, so locally compact Hausdorff, second countable). For g∈C_c(X,H) let g̃:=c⁻¹∘g on U, 0 off U (continuous, spt g⊆U compact). Fix compact C⊇spt g in U and open W⊇C, W⊂⊂U (e.g. W:=thickening δ C, 2δ<infDist(C,ℝ^P∖U), δ:=1 if U=ℝ^P; if C=∅, g=0 and L(g):=0). With a standard mollifier φ_σ (C^∞, ≥0, ∫φ_σ=1, support in B̄_σ) and 0<σ<dist(C,ℝ^P∖W), g_σ:=g̃∗φ_σ (componentwise) is C^∞ with tsupport in C+B̄_σ⊆W, so g_σ∈𝒟ⁿ(U); g_σ→g̃ uniformly (uniform continuity), |g_σ|≤|g̃|_∞ (convexity of the norm). By (E1) |T(g_σ)−T(g_τ)|≤|g_σ−g_τ|_∞M_W(T)→0, so L(g):=lim_{σ↓0}T(g_σ) exists; it is independent of the mollifier and of C, W, as h_k, h'_k∈𝒟ⁿ(U) supported in a fixed open W'⊂⊂U with h_k, h'_k→g̃ uniformly have |T(h_k)−T(h'_k)|≤|h_k−h'_k|_∞M_{W'}(T)→0 (E1), and a union of two open sets ⊂⊂U is ⊂⊂U. Hence (a) L is linear; (b) L(ω|_U)=T(ω) for ω∈𝒟ⁿ(U) (constant sequence); (c) |L(g)|≤sup‖g‖_H·M_W(T) if spt g⊆W⊂⊂U, W open. So L is locally bounded (IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional: for compact C⊆X apply (c) with open W⊇C, W⊂⊂U).
3. (Riesz.) simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory (H finite-dimensional, so separable; L locally bounded) yields the Radon measure μ₀:=vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure L on X and ν : X→H, measurable for the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ₀, with ‖ν‖=1 μ₀-a.e. and L(g)=∫⟨g,ν⟩_H dμ₀ for g∈C_c(X,H); simon_theorem_4_14_positive_envelope yields, for f∈C_c(X,ℝ_{≥0}),
 (3a) sup{L(g) : g∈C_c(X,H), ‖g‖≤f} = ∫f dμ₀.
As μ₀ is σ-finite (X σ-compact), Carathéodory-measurable sets are μ₀-null-measurable (radonCaratheodoryMeasure μ₀ has the null sets of μ₀ and equals μ₀ on Borel sets), so ν=ν_B μ₀-a.e. with ν_B Borel, L(g)=∫⟨g,ν_B⟩dμ₀; set ν_B:=0 on the Borel null set {‖ν_B‖≠1}, so ‖ν_B‖≤1 everywhere.
4. μ:=push-forward of μ₀ under U ↪ ℝ^P: Borel, μ(ℝ^P∖U)=0, μ(C)=μ₀(C)<∞ for compact C⊆U. ξ(x)(α):=⟨c(α),ν_B(x)⟩_H for x∈U, ξ:=0 off U, is Borel (finite-dimensional target), so a.e. strongly measurable, and |ξ(x)(α)|≤‖c(α)‖‖ν_B(x)‖≤|α| (Cauchy–Schwarz); so |ξ(x)(ω(x))|≤|ω(x)|. For ω∈𝒟ⁿ(U), by 2(b) and 3, T(ω)=L(ω|_U)=∫_U⟨c(ω),ν_B⟩dμ₀=∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x), the integrand being bounded by the μ-integrable |ω|_∞1_{tsupport ω}.
5. (M_W(T)=μ(W), W open.) ≤: for ω admissible for M_W(T) (tsupport ω⊆W, |ω|≤1), ξ(ω)≤1_{tsupport ω}, so T(ω)≤μ(tsupport ω)<∞, ofReal T(ω)≤μ(W); take the sup. ≥: μ(W)=μ₀(W∩U)=sup{μ₀(C) : C⊆W∩U compact} (inner regularity). Fix such C, ε>0, f∈C_c(X,[0,1]) with f=1 on C, spt f⊆W∩U (Urysohn), and by (3a) g with ‖g‖≤f, L(g) ≥ ∫f dμ₀ − ε ≥ μ₀(C)−ε. Mollifying as in step 2 with σ<dist(spt f,ℝ^P∖(W∩U)): g_σ∈𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport g_σ⊆W∩U, |g_σ|≤1, T(g_σ)→L(g); for small σ, g_σ is admissible with T(g_σ)≥μ₀(C)−2ε. So M_W(T)≥μ(W) (both may be ∞).
6. (U1) Finite signed Borel measures κ, κ' on an open G with ∫b dκ=∫b dκ' for all b∈C_c^∞(G) agree on Borel subsets of G: for compact C⊆G, smooth 0≤b_k≤1, b_k ↓ 1_C, supported in a fixed compact subset of G, give κ(C)=κ'(C) (dominated convergence); compact sets form a π-system generating the Borel sets; κ, κ' are finite.
Last assertion. Assume M_W(∂T)<∞ (boundaryMassOn) for open W⊂⊂U. If n=0, μHE[0]=μH[0] is counting measure, so μHE[0](E)=0 forces E=∅. If n>P, μ=0 (step 1). Let 1≤n≤P, Hⁿ:=μHE[n].
7. Let Hⁿ(E)=0; by Borel regularity take Borel E'⊇E, Hⁿ(E')=0, and replace E by E'∩U (μ(ℝ^P∖U)=0). μ is inner regular on Borel sets (locally finite on the σ-compact Polish space U, 0 off U), so it suffices that μ(C)=0 for compact C⊆U with Hⁿ(C)=0. Fix such C and open W⊇C, W⊂⊂U (step 2): μ(W)=M_W(T)<∞, M_W(∂T)<∞.
8. (Lemma TD.) Let n≥1, m a finite signed Borel measure on ℝⁿ with compact support, Λ:=sup{|∫div g dm| : g∈C_c^∞(ℝⁿ;ℝⁿ), |g|≤1}<∞. Then |m|(N)=0 if Lⁿ(N)=0.
Proof. u_σ(y):=∫φ_σ(y−z)dm(z) (φ_σ a mollifier on ℝⁿ) is C^∞, supported in spt m+B̄_σ, with ∂_ju_σ(y)=∫∂_jφ_σ(y−z)dm(z) (differentiation under the integral, m finite). For g∈C_c^∞(ℝⁿ;ℝⁿ), by Fubini ∫∇u_σ·g dy = ∫∫∇φ_σ(y−z)·g(y)dy dm(z) = −∫div(φ̌_σ∗g)dm, where (φ̌_σ∗g)(z):=∫φ_σ(y−z)g(y)dy is C_c^∞ with |φ̌_σ∗g|≤1 if |g|≤1; so |∫∇u_σ·g|≤Λ, whence, ∇u_σ being C_c^∞, ∫|∇u_σ|≤Λ (test g_k:=χ_k∇u_σ/(|∇u_σ|²+1/k)^{1/2}, smooth cut-offs χ_k ↑ 1, |g_k|≤1; monotone convergence). If n≥2, Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev (Mathlib eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one, p=n/(n−1) conjugate to finrank ℝⁿ=n, ‖fderiv u_σ‖=|∇u_σ|) gives ‖u_σ‖_{L^{n/(n−1)}}≤C_nΛ; if n=1, u_σ(y)=∫_{−∞}^yu_σ' gives sup|u_σ|≤Λ. For a∈C_c^∞(ℝⁿ), by Fubini ∫u_σa dy = ∫(φ̌_σ∗a)dm → ∫a dm as σ ↓ 0 (φ̌_σ∗a→a uniformly, |m| finite), so by Hölder |∫a dm|≤C_nΛ‖a‖_{L^n}, resp. Λ‖a‖_{L¹} (n=1). For open G, |m|(G)=sup{∫a dm : a∈C_c^∞(G), |a|≤1} (Hahn decomposition S₊∪S₋, inner regularity of |m| on G, smooth approximation of 1_{S₊∩C}−1_{S₋∩C} for compact C, dominated convergence), so |m|(G)≤C_nΛLⁿ(G)^{1/n}, resp. ΛL¹(G). Outer regularity of Lⁿ gives open G⊇N of arbitrarily small measure, so |m|(N)=0.
9. (Projection; Simon 2.36.) For α=(i_1<⋯<i_n)∈𝕀 let p_α be as in (E2), dx^α:=dx^{i_1}∧⋯∧dx^{i_n}. p_α is 1-Lipschitz, so Hⁿ(p_α(C))≤Hⁿ(C)=0, and Hⁿ=Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (μHE[n] on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is volume): N_α:=p_α(C) is compact, Lⁿ-null. dλ_α:=⟨dx^α,ξ⟩dμ⌞W is a finite signed Borel measure on W (|⟨dx^α,ξ⟩|≤|dx^α|=1, μ(W)<∞); for b∈C_c^∞(W), m_{α,b}:=(p_α)_*(bλ_α) is finite, supported in the compact p_α(spt b). For g∈C_c^∞(ℝⁿ;ℝⁿ), γ:=Σ_jg_jε_j with ε_j:=(−1)^{j−1}dy¹∧⋯∧dy^{j−1}∧dy^{j+1}∧⋯∧dyⁿ has dγ=(div g)dy, |γ(y)|=|g(y)|, p_α^#((div g)dy)=d(p_α^#γ); so step 4 for the test form b·p_α^#((div g)dy) (support in spt b⊆W) gives
 ∫div g dm_{α,b} = ∫b(x)(div g)(p_αx)⟨dx^α,ξ(x)⟩dμ(x) = T(b·d(p_α^#γ)) = T(d(bp_α^#γ)) − T(db∧p_α^#γ) = ∂T(bp_α^#γ) − T(db∧p_α^#γ),
of absolute value ≤ |b|_∞M_W(∂T)+|db|_∞M_W(T)<∞ if |g|≤1, by (E1), (E2) (|p_α^#γ|=|γ|≤1, |db∧p_α^#γ|≤|db|). By step 8, |m_{α,b}|(N_α)=0, i.e. ∫_{p_α⁻¹(N_α)}b dλ_α = m_{α,b}(N_α) = 0 for all b∈C_c^∞(W). (U1) for 1_{p_α⁻¹(N_α)}λ_α and 0 on W gives λ_α(B∩p_α⁻¹(N_α))=0 for Borel B⊆W; as C⊆p_α⁻¹(N_α), ∫_Ch dλ_α=0 for bounded Borel h on W.
10. For ω admissible for M_W(T), ω=Σ_{α∈𝕀}ω_αdx^α with ω_α∈C_c^∞(W); by steps 4, 9 (h:=ω_α) and |ξ(ω)|≤|ω|≤1,
 T(ω) = Σ_α∫ω_αdλ_α = Σ_α∫_Cω_αdλ_α + ∫_{W∖C}ξ(ω)dμ = ∫_{W∖C}ξ(ω)dμ ≤ μ(W∖C).
Taking the sup, μ(W)=M_W(T)≤μ(W∖C)<∞ gives μ(C)=0, so μ(E)=0 (step 7).
Part (IMC). Hⁿ:=μHE[n]; IMReps are written (carrier, mult, orient)=(M,θ,ξ); η_{x,r}(y):=r⁻¹(y−x) (blowUpMap); 𝒯(N,x,Q):=HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q; 𝒰(ζ,Q):=IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P0) SimonGMT's density theorems use simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n=μHE[n] (n∈ℕ), so null sets, finiteness and densities transfer; Hⁿ is Borel regular.
(P1) Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A))=r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) for all A (scaling, isometry invariance), so ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)}f dHⁿ=r^{−n}∫_Af∘η_{x,r}dHⁿ for Borel A, bounded Borel f.
(P2) (simon_theorem_3_6 with (P0)) If D is Borel, Hⁿ(D)<∞, then Hⁿ(D∩B̄_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ)→0 as r ↓ 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x∉D.
(P3) (Cauchy–Binet) det(ABᵀ)=Σ_{I∈𝕀}det(A_I)det(B_I) for n×P matrices A, B (A_I: columns I of A): expanding det(ABᵀ) multilinearly in its columns Σ_kB_{jk}A_{·k}, terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the rest by the increasing rearrangement I (k=I∘σ) gives Σ_Idet(A_I)Σ_σsgn(σ)Π_jB_{j,I_{σ(j)}}=Σ_Idet(A_I)det(B_I). (n>P: 𝕀=∅, rank ABᵀ<n.)
(P4) If τ_1,…,τ_n are orthonormal and ⟨α,ζ⟩=±α(τ) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α,ζ⟩|≤|α|: with A_{ik}:=⟨τ_i,e_k⟩, α(τ)=Σ_Idet(A_I)α(e_I) (multilinear, alternating), so by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3) |α(τ)|≤|α|(Σ_Idet(A_I)²)^{1/2}=|α|det(AAᵀ)^{1/2}=|α|, as AAᵀ=(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩)=id. (n=0: |α(∅)|=|α|.)
(P5) Orthonormal bases τ, τ' of an n-dimensional Q satisfy τ'_i=Σ_jO_{ij}τ_j, O orthogonal, so α(τ')=det(O)α(τ)=±α(τ) for alternating α. Hence 𝒰(ζ,Q)∧𝒰(ζ',Q) ⇒ ζ'=±ζ, and 𝒰(ζ,Q) ⇒ 𝒰(−ζ,Q).
(P6) For an IMRep (M,θ,ξ) in open U and compact K⊆U, Hⁿ(M∩K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ≥1 on M).
(d) For Hⁿ-a.e. x∈R.carrier some Q has 𝒰(R.orient x, Q) (orientation field), i.e. ⟨α, R.orient x⟩=±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ and all α; so |R.orient x α|≤|α| by (P4).
(a) Let D:=M'∖M.
1. For R∈ℕ, U_R:={x∈U : |x|<R, infDist(x,ℝ^P∖U)>1/R} ({|x|<R} if U=ℝ^P) is open with compact closure in U, U_R ↑ U. D_R:=D∩U_R is Borel, Hⁿ(D_R)≤Hⁿ(M'∩closure U_R)<∞, so by (P2) some Hⁿ-null Z_R has Hⁿ(D_R∩B̄_r(x))=o(rⁿ) for x∉D_R∪Z_R. Let Z'⊇⋃_RZ_R be Borel, Hⁿ-null (P0). For x∈M∖Z' choose R, r₀>0 with B̄_{r₀}(x)⊆U_R; then x∉D_R (x∈M) and D∩B̄_r(x)=D_R∩B̄_r(x) for r<r₀, so Hⁿ(D∩B̄_r(x))=o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q, f∈C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f⊆B_ρ(0). For r<r₀/ρ, η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure (genuine Bochner integrals), η_{x,r}(M')=η_{x,r}(M)⊔η_{x,r}(D) (η_{x,r} injective), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')}f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)}f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)}f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞r^{−n}Hⁿ(D∩B_{rρ}(x)) → 0.
So both families have the same limit as r→0⁺ or both have none, and finrank Q=n is common: 𝒯(M,x,Q)↔𝒯(M',x,Q) for x∈M∖Z' and all Q; M∩Z' is Hⁿ⌞M-null.

subproblem.title: Slicing by Lipschitz functions: the restricted currents, the support of slices and the slice mass bounds (Simon 6.4.6–4.11)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), and suppose T and ∂T are represented by measures: there are Borel measures μ, μ' on ℝ^P, finite on compact subsets of U, and a.e. strongly measurable fields ξ (of (k+1)-vectors), ξ' (of k-vectors) with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ'-a.e. x (Euclidean coefficient norm), T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω) dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and ∂T(η) = ∫ξ'(η) dμ' for η ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be Lipschitz with constant L. Then there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' (Simon's T⌞{f < t} and (∂T)⌞{f < t}), such that the slice Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t satisfies: (∂A_t)(η) = B_t(η), i.e. Z_t(η) = 0, whenever η ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and tsupport η is disjoint from {f = t}; for every open W and t, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0⁺} h⁻¹ μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}); and for every open W and a, b ∈ ℝ, the lower integral ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(Z_t) dt ≤ L · μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 6.4.6–4.11 (4.8–4.9 are printed for f∈C¹, via 4.11, with the instruction to use f^{(σ)} and let σ↓0; that limit is done in step 3). Restrictions are taken w.r.t. the given representations (μ,ξ) of T and (μ',ξ') of ∂T (Simon 2.9): A_t=T⌞{f<t}, B_t=(∂T)⌞{f<t}, Z_t=∂A_t−B_t=⟨T,f,t₋⟩.
Notation: |α|:=covectorEuclideanNorm α, |ω|_∞:=sup_x|ω(x)|. (E1) |β∧γ|≤|β||γ| for a 1-covector β and a k-covector γ: k!|γ|²=Σ_{i_1,…,i_k}γ(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_k})² is the basis-independent Hilbert–Schmidt norm of γ, so |·| is invariant under orthogonal coordinate changes; rotate so that β=|β|e¹, then β∧γ=|β|Σ_{I∌1}γ_Ie¹∧e^I has norm ≤|β||γ|. (E2) By hypothesis |ξ(x)(α)|≤|α| μ-a.e. and |ξ'(x)(α)|≤|α| μ'-a.e.
1. (Restricted currents.) For Borel E and ω∈𝒟^{k+1}(U) let A_E(ω):=∫_Eξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x). The integrand is a.e. strongly measurable (ξ composed with the continuous pairing) and by (E2) bounded μ-a.e. by |ω|_∞1_{tsupport ω}, with μ(tsupport ω)<∞ (compact in U); so it is integrable, and A_E is linear. If ω_j→0 in 𝒟^{k+1}(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K⊆U, uniform convergence of the forms and all derivatives; |·| is equivalent to any norm on covectors), |A_E(ω_j)|≤|ω_j|_∞μ(K)→0, so A_E∈𝒟_{k+1}(U). Likewise B_E(η):=∫_Eξ'(η)dμ' gives B_E∈𝒟_k(U). A_t:=A_{{f<t}}, B_t:=B_{{f<t}} ({f<t} is open, f being continuous) satisfy the first two conclusions; T=A_{ℝ^P}, ∂T=B_{ℝ^P} by the representation hypotheses.
2. (Support.) Let η∈𝒟^k(U), K:=tsupport η disjoint from {f=t}. K₋:=K∩{f<t}, K₊:=K∩{f>t} are disjoint compact sets with union K. Take χ∈C^∞(ℝ^P;[0,1]) with χ=1 near K₋, χ=0 near K₊; η₋:=χη, η₊:=(1−χ)η are test forms in U, η=η₋+η₊, and tsupport η_±⊆K_± (η_± vanishes near K_∓ and off K). As η₊, dη₊ vanish on {f<t}, (∂A_t)(η₊)=A_t(dη₊)=∫_{f<t}ξ(dη₊)dμ=0 and B_t(η₊)=∫_{f<t}ξ'(η₊)dμ'=0. As η₋, dη₋ vanish off {f<t}, (∂A_t)(η₋)=∫_{f<t}ξ(dη₋)dμ=∫ξ(dη₋)dμ=T(dη₋)=∂T(η₋)=∫ξ'(η₋)dμ'=∫_{f<t}ξ'(η₋)dμ'=B_t(η₋). Adding gives (A_t).boundary η=B_t η, the third conclusion.
3. (Pointwise bound; Simon 4.9 for Lipschitz f.) Fix t, open W, 0<h<1, ε:=h²/8. Take C^∞ nonincreasing γ:ℝ→[0,1] with γ=1 on (−∞,t−h+ε], γ=0 on [t−ε,∞), |γ'|≤1/(h−4ε) (mollify at scale <ε the piecewise linear function equal to 1 on (−∞,t−h+2ε], 0 on [t−2ε,∞), linear between). f_σ:=f∗φ_σ (φ_σ a standard mollifier) is C^∞, |∇f_σ|≤L, |f_σ−f|≤Lσ. For Lσ<ε let g_σ:=γ∘f_σ (C^∞, [0,1]-valued, derivatives bounded on compacts), g:=γ∘f (continuous).
(i) For η∈𝒟^k(U), g_σdη and g_ση are test forms in U and d(g_ση)=dg_σ∧η+g_σdη, so T(g_σdη)−∂T(g_ση)=T(g_σdη)−T(d(g_ση))=−T(dg_σ∧η).
(ii) dg_σ=γ'(f_σ)df_σ vanishes unless t−h+ε<f_σ<t−ε, which forces t−h<f<t (as |f_σ−f|<ε); |dg_σ|≤L/(h−4ε). By the representation of T, (E1), (E2): if tsupport η⊆W, |η|≤1, then |T(dg_σ∧η)|≤∫|dg_σ||η|dμ≤(L/(h−4ε))μ(W∩{t−h<f<t}).
(iii) As σ↓0, g_σ→g uniformly (γ Lipschitz, f_σ→f uniformly), so T(g_σdη)→∫gξ(dη)dμ and ∂T(g_ση)→∫gξ'(η)dμ' (dominated convergence on the compact tsupport η, of finite μ- and μ'-measure). So, writing g_h:=γ_h∘f to record the dependence on h, and as h−4ε=h(1−h/2), for admissible η (tsupport η⊆W, |η|≤1):
 ∫g_hξ(dη)dμ − ∫g_hξ'(η)dμ' ≤ (L/(h(1−h/2)))μ(W∩{t−h<f<t}).
(iv) As h↓0, g_h→1_{{f<t}} pointwise (if f(x)<t, then f(x)≤t−h+ε once h≤t−f(x), so g_h(x)=1; if f(x)≥t, then f(x)≥t−ε and g_h(x)=0). By dominated convergence ∫g_hξ(dη)dμ→∫_{f<t}ξ(dη)dμ=(∂A_t)(η) and ∫g_hξ'(η)dμ'→B_t(η). Along h_i↓0 realizing liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W∩{t−h<f<t}), with (1−h/2)⁻¹→1, this gives Z_t(η)=(∂A_t−B_t)(η)≤L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W∩{t−h<f<t}) for admissible η, so M_W(Z_t)=sup ofReal(Z_t(η))≤L·liminf_{h→0⁺}ofReal(h⁻¹)μ(W∩{t−h<f<t}) in [0,∞], the fourth conclusion. (Read (ii)–(iv) in [0,∞]; the integrals are finite since only tsupport η matters, e.g. μ(tsupport η∩{t−h<f<t})<∞ may replace μ(W∩{t−h<f<t}) in (ii). If L=0, f is constant, {t−h<f<t}=∅ for small h, the bound in (ii) is 0 and Z_t=0, so 0·∞=0 is harmless; if the liminf is ∞, then L>0 and the claim is trivial.)
4. (Integral bound; Simon 4.10.) Fix open W and a, b. If a≥b, Ioo a b=∅ and there is nothing to prove; let a<b. If L=0, M_W(Z_t)=0 for all t (step 3). If L>0 and μ(W∩{a<f<b})=∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise F(s):=μ(W∩{a<f<s}) for s≤b, F(s):=F(b) for s>b, is real, bounded, nondecreasing, F=0 on (−∞,a]. For t∈(a,b), 0<h<t−a, {t−h<f<t}⊆{a<f<t}∖{a<f<t−h}, so μ(W∩{t−h<f<t})≤F(t)−F(t−h). F is differentiable a.e. (Lebesgue, Monotone.ae_differentiableAt), and there step 3 gives M_W(Z_t)≤LF'(t). By lintegral_mono_ae (no measurability of t↦M_W(Z_t) needed for the lower integral), ∫⁻_{(a,b)}M_W(Z_t)dt≤L∫⁻_{(a,b)}F'(t)dt. Finally ∫_{(a,b)}F'≤F(b)−F(a)=μ(W∩{a<f<b}) (F(a)=0) by MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc: F'=deriv F≥0 a.e. is integrable on [a,b] (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv) with interval integral in [0,F(b)−F(a)]. This is the fifth conclusion.

Support: split η into parts supported in {f<t} and {f>t}; ∂A_t and B_t agree on each.
Pointwise bound: cut-offs γ∘f_σ give T(g_σdη)−∂T(g_ση)=−T(dg_σ∧η), at most L/(h−4ε)·μ(W∩{t−h<f<t}); let σ↓0, then h↓0.
Integral bound: pointwise bound ≤LF'(t) for monotone F(s)=μ(W∩{a<f<s}); integrate, ∫F'≤F(b)−F(a).

subproblem.statement: Let m, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k, n := m + 1, P := n + k; let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, N ⊆ ℝ^P an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N) with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N (IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N)) with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T). Assume moreover (hmon): for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ ≥ 0 such that for all y ∈ ℝ^P and R ∈ ℝ with closedBall(y, R) ⊆ K the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (in [0, ∞]) is monotone on (0, R) — this is conclusion (i) of the monotonicity theorem dimred_minimizing_monotonicity for P = n + k and d = n + ℓ. Let x ∈ U, let x_j ∈ ℝ^P with x_j → x, and let λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0. Write η_j := dilation x_j λ_j (η_j(y) = λ_j⁻¹(y − x_j)), U_j := η_j(U), A_j := η_j(U ∩ N) and S_j := blowUp T x_j λ_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j). Part I (one dilation). a ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0, η := dilation a λ, Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U), η_#Y := blowUp Y a λ ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)).

Part II.
1. ((1)) U_j = η_j(U) is open, as η_j is a homeomorphism and U is open.
2. ((2)) If R < 0, closedBall(0, R) = ∅. If R ≥ 0, |x_j − x| < r and λ_jR ≤ r (all large j), each z ∈ closedBall(0, R) has |x_j + λ_jz − x| ≤ |x_j − x| + λ_jR < 2r, so x_j + λ_jz ∈ U and z = η_j(x_j + λ_jz) ∈ U_j.
3. ((3), (4), (6)) (S5) with Y := T, A := U ∩ N gives IsMinimizingIn S_j A_j; (S2): spt S_j = η_j(spt T) ⊆ A_j (spt T ⊆ U ∩ N); (S3) with BoundaryVanishes T: S_j.boundary = 0.

subproblem.statement: For all P, m ∈ ℕ (degree n := m + 1) there is a constant c ∈ ℝ≥0 with c ≥ 1 such that for every ρ > 0, every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and every Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 there is a finite set 𝒬 of currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with the following property. If T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, spt T ⊆ K, M(T) ≤ Λ and M(∂T) < ∞, then there are Q ∈ 𝒬, R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that: Q, ∂Q and R are integer multiplicity; T − Q − S = ∂R; Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρⁿ; M(Q) ≤ c·M(T), M(∂Q) ≤ c·M(∂T), M(R) ≤ c·ρ·M(T) and M(S) ≤ c·ρ·M(∂T); spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√P·ρ, spt T) and spt ∂Q ∪ spt S ⊆ thickening(3√P·ρ, spt ∂T), where thickening(r, A) := {x : |x − y| < r for some y ∈ A} (Mathlib Metric.thickening; it is empty when A = ∅). Here M := massOn ℝ^P is the total mass (GeometricCurrentOn.mass, with the Euclidean coefficient norm), masses and products are read in [0, ∞], and spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Nothing beyond these properties is asserted about Q: in particular the statement does not assert that Q is a polyhedral chain (that is only a feature of the construction used in the proof).

subproblem.title: Minimality of the limit and convergence of the mass measures for all representations (Simon 7.2.4 (8), (12)–(14))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be open and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity. Assume (1) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly: currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Then C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ) and μ_{S_j} → μ_C for all integer multiplicity representations (MassMeasuresConverge S C: for all IMReps R_j of S_j in U_j and R of C in ℝ^P and every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ f dR_j.measure → ∫ f dR.measure).

Source: Simon 7.2.4, (8), (12)–(14). Siblings used: vanish_off_support (VO); mass_and_support, first conjunct (MR). M_O(Y) := Y.massOn O; IM: integer multiplicity.
0. (L1) For Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and any O, M_O(Y) = M_{O∩V}(Y): admissible forms are test forms in V (tsupport ⊆ V), so the admissible sets coincide.
(L2) If V is open and R_Y represents Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V), M_O(Y) = R_Y.measure O for open O ⊆ ℝ^P (MR).
(L3) For bounded open O and strictly increasing φ'', M_O(C) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ''(i)}). For ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n O: closure O ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R, so by (1) tsupport ω ⊆ O ⊆ U_j for large j, whence ofReal(currentEval(S_j, ω)) = ofReal(S_j(ω_j)) ≤ M_O(S_j), ω_j being ω as an element of massAdmissibleOn U_j n O; by (2), ofReal(C(ω)) = lim_i ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ''(i)}, ω)) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ''(i)}). Take the sup over ω.
(L4) If R_k represents A_k ∈ 𝒟_n(V_k) (k = 1, 2; V_k open), ρ_k := R_k.measure, O ⊆ V₁ ∩ V₂ is open and currentEval A₁ ω = currentEval A₂ ω whenever tsupport ω ⊆ O, then ρ₁(E) = ρ₂(E) for Borel E ⊆ O. (i) For open G ⊆ O, M_G(A₁) and M_G(A₂) have the same admissible forms (tsupport ⊆ G ⊆ V₁ ∩ V₂) with equal values, so ρ₁(G) = ρ₂(G) by (L2). (ii) If G is open and closure G ⊆ O is compact, ρ_k(G) ≤ ∫_{carrier∩closure G} mult dHⁿ < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult). (iii) O_q := ball(0, q) ∖ cthickening(1/q, ℝ^P ∖ O) (ball(0, q) if O = ℝ^P), q ≥ 1, are open, increasing, with compact closures in O and union O. The measures ρ_k⌞O_q, finite by (ii), agree on every open G (G ∩ O_q is open ⊆ O; (i)) and on ℝ^P; open sets are a π-system generating the Borel sets, so they are equal (ext_of_generate_finite). (iv) For Borel E ⊆ O, ρ_k(E) = lim_q ρ_k(E ∩ O_q) (continuity from below), equal for k = 1, 2 by (iii).
1. (Minimality.) C is IM. Let W be open with CompactlyContained W univ and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) IM with SameBoundary S C, K := (S − C).support compact and K ⊆ univ ∩ W. Choose ε > 0 with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W (IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open). Hypothesis (3) with K, ε, ψ := id and the admissible S gives an open W', K ⊆ W' ⊆ thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W, and a strictly increasing φ' with limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S); W' is bounded, so by (L3) M_{W'}(C) ≤ liminf_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ limsup_i ⋯ ≤ M_{W'}(S). Let R_C, R_S represent C, S, μ_C := R_C.measure, μ_S := R_S.measure. If tsupport ω ⊆ O := ℝ^P ∖ K (open), then (S − C)(ω) = 0 by (VO), i.e. currentEval(S, ω) = currentEval(C, ω); so by (L4) (V₁ = V₂ = ℝ^P) μ_S = μ_C on Borel subsets of O ⊇ W ∖ W' (K ⊆ W'). By (L2), M_W(C) = μ_C(W') + μ_C(W ∖ W') = M_{W'}(C) + μ_S(W ∖ W') ≤ M_{W'}(S) + μ_S(W ∖ W') = μ_S(W) = M_W(S). Hence IsMinimizingIn C univ.
2. (Radon criterion.) Claim: if μ, μ_j are Borel measures on ℝ^P with (a) μ(K) < ∞ and (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K, and (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for bounded open G, then ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ (Bochner) for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Proof. K₀ := tsupport f (compact), M₀ := sup|f|; if M₀ = 0 all integrals vanish. (i) By (a), (b) there is j₁ with μ_j(K₀) ≤ A := μ(K₀) + 1 < ∞ for j ≥ j₁; f is ν-integrable for ν ∈ {μ} ∪ {μ_j : j ≥ j₁} (Borel, |f| ≤ M₀1_{K₀}). (ii) As f = f⁺ − f⁻ and finitely many j do not matter, it suffices to treat continuous 0 ≤ g ≤ M₀ vanishing off K₀. (iii) Layer cake (lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt, _le): for Borel ν, I(ν) := ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dν = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ν({g > t}) dt = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ν({g ≥ t}) dt; for t > 0, {g > t} is bounded open and {g ≥ t} ⊆ K₀ compact, both empty for t > M₀. (iv) By (c) and Fatou (lintegral_liminf_le), I(μ) ≤ ∫⁻ liminf_j μ_j({g > t}) dt ≤ liminf_j I(μ_j). (v) For j ≥ j₁, μ_j({g ≥ t}) ≤ A·1_{(0,M₀]}(t), integrable; reverse Fatou (limsup_lintegral_le for (μ_{j₁+i})_i, whose t-functions are antitone, hence measurable) and (b) give limsup_j I(μ_j) ≤ ∫⁻ limsup_j μ_j({g ≥ t}) dt ≤ ∫⁻ μ({g ≥ t}) dt = I(μ). (vi) So I(μ_j) → I(μ) ≤ M₀μ(K₀) < ∞, with I(μ_j) ≤ M₀A for j ≥ j₁; as ∫ g dν = I(ν).toReal for integrable g ≥ 0 (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae) and toReal is continuous at finite values, ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ; recombine f⁺, f⁻. ∎
3. (Mass measures.) Let R_j, R represent S_j (every j), C; μ_j := R_j.measure, μ := R.measure; f continuous with compact support. We check (a)–(c) of step 2. (a) For compact K ⊆ univ, μ(K) = ∫⁻_{carrier∩K} mult dHⁿ < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult). (c) For bounded open G, μ(G) = M_G(C) ≤ liminf_j M_G(S_j) = liminf_j μ_j(G) ((L2), (L3) with φ'' = id). (b) Let K be compact, ε > 0, a := μ(thickening(ε, K)). If limsup_j μ_j(K) > b > a, then μ_j(K) > b infinitely often, so μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b ∀i for a strictly increasing ψ (extraction_of_frequently_atTop). Hypothesis (3) with K, ε, ψ and S := C, which is admissible (C is IM; SameBoundary C C is True for n = 0, reflexivity otherwise; C − C = 0 vanishes on every ball, an open set with compact closure, so its support is empty), gives an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' with limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(C) = μ(W) ≤ a. But M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) = μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(K) > b for all i (L2), so that lim sup is ≥ b > a, a contradiction. Thus limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) for all ε > 0. As K is closed, thickening(1/q, K) ↓ K and μ(thickening(1, K)) ≤ μ(cthickening(1, K)) < ∞ by (a) (compact), so μ(thickening(1/q, K)) → μ(K) (tendsto_measure_thickening_of_isClosed); hence limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).
Step 2 gives ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ for all representations and f: MassMeasuresConverge Ss C; with step 1 the claim follows. ∎
proof_key_steps: (L1)–(L4): mass on open sets = weight of any IMRep; M_O(C) ≤ liminf M_O(S_j) for bounded open O; currents agreeing near O have equal weights in O.
Minimality: (3), (L3) give M_{W'}(C) ≤ M_{W'}(S); by (VO), (L4) the weights of S, C agree on W ∖ W'.
Radon criterion: layer cake, Fatou, reverse Fatou.
Mass measures: lim inf bound on bounded open sets by (L3); lim sup bound on compacts by contradiction with competitor C, ε ↓ 0; apply the criterion.

subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O) with ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L (operator norm of fderiv ℝ f y) for every y ∈ O. Then there is a map push : 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (currents GeometricCurrentOn univ n) such that: (A) for every integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) whose support spt Y is compact and contained in O, and every integer multiplicity representation R = (M, θ, ξ) of Y (IMRep univ n, R.Represents Y): (i) push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)((ω(f(x))) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every test form ω, where (ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x))(v₁, …, vₙ) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)v₁, …, Df(x)vₙ) (Lean: (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) and Hⁿ = μHE[n] — this is Simon 2.24(2), f_#Y(ω) = ∫⟨ω(f(x)), Λₙdf_x ξ(x)⟩θ dHⁿ; (ii) push Y is integer multiplicity; (iii) spt(push Y) ⊆ f(spt Y); (iv) M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y) (total masses, ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ n) * Y.mass); (v) if ∂Y = 0 then ∂(push Y) = 0; (vi) if f(y) = y for every y ∈ spt Y, then push Y = Y; and (B) push(Y₁ − Y₂) = push Y₁ − push Y₂ for all integer multiplicity Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact supports contained in O.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 6.2.23–2.24, 6.3.3–3.9 (integrality sketch 3.5–3.8 replaced by steps 9–11). Siblings: (VO) vanish_off_support; (MR) mass_and_support (first conjunct); (IMC)(a)–(d) foundations.
Notation. n := m+1; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; IM := integer multiplicity; currents live in ℝ^P (domain univ); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, |ω|_∞ := sup_x|ω(x)|; for an IMRep R = (M,θ,ξ), μ_R := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For x ∈ O, (f^#ω)(x) := (ω(f(x))).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)·,…,Df(x)·). Y is admissible if it is IM with spt Y compact ⊆ O. Unless said otherwise, Y is admissible, R = (M,θ,ξ) an IMRep of Y, K := spt Y.
Algebra. (L0) For a k-covector β, ‖β‖²_HS := Σ_{i₁,…,i_k}β(e_{i₁},…,e_{i_k})² = k!|β|² (Hilbert–Schmidt norm; each increasing tuple occurs k! times up to sign, repeated indices give 0); ‖·‖_HS is invariant under orthogonal changes of basis. (L1) For linear A and an n-covector α, |α∘ΛⁿA| ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ|α|, (α∘ΛⁿA)(v) := α(Av₁,…,Avₙ): replacing one slot of a multilinear γ by A multiplies ‖γ‖_HS by at most ‖A‖ (other arguments fixed, Σ_iγ(Ae_i,…)² = |Aᵀg|² ≤ ‖A‖²|g|², g representing γ(·,…)); repeat n times, use (L0). (L2) For orthonormal τ₁,…,τₙ, |β(τ)| ≤ |β| (rotate τ_i to e_i by (L0); β(τ) is then a coordinate of β). So if ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ), τ orthonormal, then |ξ(x)(α∘ΛⁿA)| ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ|α|.
Proof.
1. (Finite mass.) Forms admissible for M_{ℝ^P∖K}(Y) have tsupport disjoint from K, so Y kills them (VO); by (MR) μ_R(ℝ^P∖K) = 0, so Hⁿ(M∖K) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M). By locallyIntegrable_mult (K compact) and (MR), Y.mass = μ_R(ℝ^P) = μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞. By R.orients (IsUnitOrientationOf), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M (good x) ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ) for all β, for some orthonormal τ.
2. (Extension.) For a bounded Borel n-form γ continuous on an open O' ⊇ K let Ȳ_R(γ) := ∫_M θξ(γ) dHⁿ (absolutely convergent: |ξ(x)(γ(x))| ≤ |γ|_∞ at good x by (L2), μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞). Claim: Ȳ_R(γ) depends only on Y and γ|_V (V any neighbourhood of K), not on R; and if R, R₁, R₂ represent Y₁−Y₂, Y₁, Y₂ (all admissible, step 6), Ȳ_R(γ) = Ȳ₁_{R₁}(γ) − Ȳ₂_{R₂}(γ). Proof: only x ∈ K matter (step 1), so Ȳ_R(γ) = Ȳ_R(χγ) for χ ∈ C_c^∞(V∩O'; [0,1]) with χ = 1 near K; χγ (0 outside) is continuous, compactly supported. γ_σ := (χγ)∗φ_σ (componentwise mollification) are test forms, γ_σ → χγ uniformly, |γ_σ|_∞ ≤ |χγ|_∞. Ȳ_R(γ_σ) = Y(γ_σ) (representation) is independent of R and additive in the current, and Ȳ_R(γ_σ) → Ȳ_R(χγ) by dominated convergence (bound |χγ|_∞θ, μ_R finite); so Ȳ_R(γ) = lim_σY(γ_σ) has both properties. Write Ȳ(γ).
3. (Definition.) By choice: for admissible Y, push Y(ω) := Ȳ(f^#ω) (continuous on the open O ⊇ K as f is C¹ there; 0 off O, harmless by step 2); otherwise push Y := 0. By step 2, push Y(ω) = ∫_M θξ(f^#ω) dHⁿ for every IMRep R of Y: the formula. (Lean: the integrand is evaluated on all of R.carrier, f arbitrary off O; but Hⁿ-a.e. point of R.carrier lies in K ⊆ O (step 1), where it is θξ(f^#ω), a.e. strongly measurable (continuous data composed with ξ), ≤ Lⁿ|ω|_∞θ (step 4); so the Bochner integral is no junk value.)
4. (Current; mass.) push Y is linear. For good x ∈ K ⊆ O, (L2), (L1) with A := Df(x) give |ξ(x)((f^#ω)(x))| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ⁿ|ω(f(x))| ≤ Lⁿ|ω|_∞ (L ≥ 0 if O ≠ ∅; if O = ∅, K = ∅, Y = 0 by VO and push Y = 0). So |push Y(ω)| ≤ Lⁿ|ω|_∞Y.mass. For |ω| ≤ 1, push Y(ω) ≤ LⁿY.mass, so ENNReal.ofReal(push Y(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(L^{m+1})·Y.mass; take the supremum.
5. (Support.) f(K) is compact (f continuous on O). If tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅, ω(f(x)) = 0 on K, so push Y(ω) = 0 (step 1). For y ∉ f(K) take r > 0 with closedBall(y,r) ∩ f(K) = ∅: push Y kills test forms supported in B_r(y) (compact closure), so y ∉ spt(push Y).
6. (Linearity.) Let Y₁, Y₂ be IM with compact supports in O. Y₁−Y₂ is IM (IMC(c)) and spt(Y₁−Y₂) ⊆ spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂ (outside both, a ball where both vanish), compact ⊆ O (supports in univ are closed). So all three are admissible and step 2 (additivity, γ := f^#ω) gives push(Y₁−Y₂)(ω) = push Y₁(ω) − push Y₂(ω); conclude by extensionality (subtraction is pointwise).
7. (Identity.) Let f(y) = y on K; Hⁿ(M∖K) = 0 (step 1). By IMC(a) (U := ℝ^P, Borel M∩K ⊆ M, Hⁿ(M∩K') ≤ μ_R(K') < ∞ for compact K'), Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M∩K is good with Q := T_xM (ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ), τ an orthonormal basis of Q) and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ K) x Q; fix one. Secant claim: each unit v ∈ Q is a limit of (z_k−x)/|z_k−x|, z_k ∈ (M∩K)∖{x}, z_k → x. Else for some ε', r' > 0 no z ∈ M∩K with 0 < |z−x| < r' has |(z−x)/|z−x| − v| < ε'. (IMC) foundations, conjunct (IMC): (b) Borel restrictions of IMReps are IMReps (of some current); (c) IM currents in an open set are closed under −, hence + (0 = X − X) and integer combinations; (d) |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e. on the carrier of an IMRep R, so (R.measure, R.orient) is a representation for (SL). subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be open and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j) be integer multiplicity with ∂S_j = 0 in U_j (S_j.boundary = 0). Assume (i) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (ii) for every R ∈ ℝ there is c ∈ [0, ∞) with M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ c for all large j. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ, an integer multiplicity C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), integer multiplicity currents Ŝ_i ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and radii ρ_i ∈ ℝ (i ∈ ℕ) such that: ∂C = 0; S_{φ(i)} ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); sup_i (M_W(Ŝ_i) + M_W(∂Ŝ_i)) < ∞ for every bounded open W ⊆ ℝ^P; Ŝ_i ⇀ C (WeaklyConvergesOn); ρ_i → ∞; closedBall(0, ρ_i) ⊆ U_{φ(i)}; and Ŝ_i(ω) = currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ_i}(0).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.15, 3.11, 4.6, 4.10, truncating at good slicing radii instead of gluing over balls.
Siblings: mass_and_support, first conjunct (MR); foundations (IMC)(b),(d); slicing (SL); closure_and_boundary_rectifiability (CL).
Notation: n := m + 1, B_r := ball(0, r), IM := integer multiplicity, |ω|_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)| (Euclidean coefficient norm). (E1) For a current X in open V, open W ⊆ V and a test form ω in V with tsupport ω ⊆ W, |X(ω)| ≤ |ω|_∞·M_W(X) (ω = 0 if |ω|_∞ = 0; else ±ω/|ω|_∞ are admissible).

1. (Radii) For integers R ≥ 1 choose J(R) ∈ ℕ, c_R ∈ [0, ∞) with closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j and M_{B_R}(S_j) ≤ c_R for j ≥ J(R) ((i), (ii)); replacing J(R) by max_{R′≤R} J(R′), J is nondecreasing. Let j₀ := J(8) and, for j ≥ j₀, R_j := max{R ∈ ℕ : 8 ≤ R ≤ max(8, j), J(R) ≤ j}. Then R_j ≥ 8, J(R_j) ≤ j, so closedBall(0, R_j) ⊆ U_j; R_j → ∞ (R_j ≥ R if R ≥ 8, j ≥ max(R, J(R))). Only j ≥ j₀ are used.
2. (Good slicing radius) Fix j ≥ j₀, an IMRep (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) of S_j and its measure μ_j = θ_jHⁿ⌞M_j, finite on compact subsets of U_j (locallyIntegrable_mult). (μ_j, ξ_j) represents S_j as in (SL): ξ_j is a.e. strongly measurable for μ_j (as for Hⁿ⌞M_j), |ξ_j(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ_j-a.e. ((IMC)(d)), S_j(ω) = ∫ ξ_j(ω) dμ_j; as S_j.boundary = 0, (μ′, ξ′) := (0, 0) represents the boundary. (SL) in U_j with f := |·| (1-Lipschitz) gives A_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), A_t(ω) = ∫_{B_t} ξ_j(ω) dμ_j = ∫_{M_j∩B_t} θ_jξ_j(ω) dHⁿ; its currents in 𝒟_m(U_j) vanish (μ′ = 0), so the slices are ∂A_t and, for W := B_{3R_j/4}, (a, b) := (R_j/4, R_j/2), ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t) dt ≤ μ_j(W ∩ {a < |y| < b}) ≤ μ_j(closedBall(0, R_j/2)) < ∞ (compact in U_j). The integrand is finite somewhere in the interval: otherwise it is ≡ ∞ there and lintegral_mono (no measurability needed) gives ∫⁻ ≥ ∞·(R_j/4) = ∞. Choose ρ′_j ∈ (R_j/4, R_j/2) with σ_j := M_{B_{3R_j/4}}(∂A_{ρ′_j}) < ∞.
3. (Truncation) R̂_j := (M_j ∩ B_{ρ′_j}, θ_j, ξ_j) is an IMRep in ℝ^P: by (IMC)(b) (in U_j, E := B_{ρ′_j}) it is one in U_j; its carrier lies in ℝ^P, ∫_{carrier∩K} θ_j dHⁿ ≤ μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ′_j)) < ∞ for compact K, other fields unchanged. By (IMC)(b) in ℝ^P (E := ℝ^P) it represents some IM Ŝ_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P): Ŝ_j(ω) = ∫_{M_j∩B_{ρ′_j}} θ_jξ_j(ω) dHⁿ.
 (a) If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ′_j}, then ω is a test form in U_j (B_{ρ′_j} ⊆ U_j), ω = 0 off B_{ρ′_j}, and Ŝ_j(ω) = ∫_{M_j} θ_jξ_j(ω) dHⁿ = S_j(ω) = currentEval(S_j, ω).
 (b) Take χ ∈ C_c^∞(B_{3R_j/4}; [0, 1]), χ = 1 near closedBall(0, ρ′_j). For β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), χβ is a test form in U_j with tsupport in B_{3R_j/4}, and d(χβ) = dβ near closedBall(0, ρ′_j) (χβ = β there; d is local: forms agreeing on an open set have equal d there). So ∂Ŝ_j(β) = Ŝ_j(dβ) = ∫_{M_j∩B_{ρ′_j}} θ_jξ_j(d(χβ)) dHⁿ = A_{ρ′_j}(d(χβ)) = ∂A_{ρ′_j}(χβ), and (E1) gives |∂Ŝ_j(β)| ≤ σ_j|χβ|_∞ ≤ σ_j|β|_∞. Hence M_O(∂Ŝ_j) ≤ σ_j for every open O.
 (c) If tsupport β ⊆ B_{ρ′_j}, then tsupport dβ ⊆ tsupport β (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so by (a) ∂Ŝ_j(β) = Ŝ_j(dβ) = S_j(dβ) = S_j.boundary(β) = 0. So M_O(∂Ŝ_j) = 0 for open O ⊆ B_{ρ′_j} (admissible forms are supported in B_{ρ′_j}).
 (d) For open O: M_O(Ŝ_j) = R̂_j.measure(O) = μ_j(O ∩ B_{ρ′_j}) ≤ μ_j(O) = M_O(S_j) ((MR) in ℝ^P and U_j).
4. (Uniform bounds) Let O be bounded open, O ⊆ B_R, R ≥ 1 an integer, j₂ ≥ max(j₀, J(R)) with ρ′_j > R for j ≥ j₂ (ρ′_j > R_j/4 → ∞). For j ≥ j₂: M_O(Ŝ_j) ≤ M_O(S_j) ≤ M_{B_R}(S_j) ≤ c_R (3(d), massOn monotone), M_O(∂Ŝ_j) = 0 (3(c)). For j₀ ≤ j < j₂: M_O(Ŝ_j) ≤ μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ′_j)) < ∞, M_O(∂Ŝ_j) ≤ σ_j < ∞. So sup_{j≥j₀}(M_O(Ŝ_j) + M_O(∂Ŝ_j)) < ∞; in particular c′_R := sup_{j≥j₀} M_{B_R}(Ŝ_j) < ∞.
5. (Weak compactness) Claim: there are strictly increasing φ, φ(i) ≥ j₀, and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with Ŝ_{φ(i)}(ω) → C(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P).
 (a) If tsupport ω ⊆ B_R, |Ŝ_j(ω)| ≤ c′_R|ω|_∞ for j ≥ j₀ (E1).
 (b) For R ∈ ℕ let 𝒯_R := {test forms ω on ℝ^P : tsupport ω ⊆ B_R}, d(ω, ω′) := |ω − ω′|_∞. Restriction to closedBall(0, R) embeds 𝒯_R into C(closedBall(0, R), Λⁿ) (Λⁿ: n-covectors, Mathlib's norm), whose sup metric is equivalent to d (covectorEuclideanNorm and Mathlib's operator norm are norms on the finite-dimensional Λⁿ). C(closedBall(0, R), Λⁿ) is second countable (ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology; on a compact domain the compact-open topology is the sup-metric one, ContinuousMap.instPseudoMetricSpace), hence separable, and so is its subset 𝒯_R: it has a countable d-dense D_R.
 (c) D := ⋃_R D_R is countable and each (Ŝ_j(ω))_{j≥j₀}, ω ∈ D, is bounded by (a); a Cantor diagonal argument gives strictly increasing φ, φ(i) ≥ j₀, with lim_i Ŝ_{φ(i)}(ω) existing for all ω ∈ D.
 (d) Each ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) has compact support, so ω ∈ 𝒯_R for some R. Given ε > 0 pick ω′ ∈ D_R with |ω − ω′|_∞ < ε; (a) for ω − ω′ gives |Ŝ_{φ(i)}(ω) − Ŝ_{φ(i′)}(ω)| ≤ 2c′_Rε + |Ŝ_{φ(i)}(ω′) − Ŝ_{φ(i′)}(ω′)|, so (Ŝ_{φ(i)}(ω))_i is Cauchy; C(ω) := its limit.
 (e) C is linear, |C(ω)| ≤ c′_R|ω|_∞ on 𝒯_R. If ω_q → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact set ⊆ some B_R, uniform convergence; norms on Λⁿ are equivalent, so |ω_q|_∞ → 0), then C(ω_q) → 0. So C is a GeometricCurrentOn univ n and Ŝ_{φ(i)} ⇀ C (WeaklyConvergesOn).
6. (C is IM) T_i := Ŝ_{φ(i)} is IM; for open W with compact closure (CompactlyContained W univ; W bounded), sup_i(M_W(T_i) + boundaryMassOn T_i W) = sup_i(M_W(T_i) + M_W(∂T_i)) < ∞ by step 4 (n = m + 1); T_i ⇀ C in U := ℝ^P. By (CL), C is IM.
7. (Output) Ŝ_i := Ŝ_{φ(i)}, ρ_i := ρ′_{φ(i)}. φ is strictly increasing; C and the Ŝ_i are IM; sup_i(M_W(Ŝ_i) + M_W(∂Ŝ_i)) < ∞ for bounded open W (step 4, fewer indices); Ŝ_i ⇀ C (step 5); ρ_i → ∞ (ρ′_j > R_j/4 → ∞); closedBall(0, ρ_i) ⊆ closedBall(0, R_{φ(i)}) ⊆ U_{φ(i)} (ρ_i < R_{φ(i)}/2); agreement is 3(a). C.boundary = 0: β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) has tsupport β ⊆ B_r for some r, and ρ_i > r for large i, so ∂Ŝ_i(β) = 0 (3(c)) and C.boundary(β) = C(dβ) = lim_i Ŝ_i(dβ) = lim_i ∂Ŝ_i(β) = 0. S_{φ(i)} ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly): if tsupport ω ⊆ B_r, then for large i, ρ_i > r and currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) = Ŝ_i(ω) (3(a)) → C(ω). ∎
proof_key_steps: 1. Radii R_j → ∞, closedBall(0, R_j) ⊆ U_j, eventual mass bounds c_R.
2. (SL) with f = |·|, μ′ = 0 and the lower integral give ρ′_j ∈ (R_j/4, R_j/2) with σ_j < ∞.
3–4. Truncation Ŝ_j: IM in ℝ^P, = S_j on B_{ρ′_j}, ∂-mass ≤ σ_j (locality of d), 0 inside; uniform bounds.
5. Separability of C(closedBall, Λⁿ) and a diagonal argument: Ŝ_{φ(i)} ⇀ C.
6–7. (CL): C is IM; agreement on growing balls: ∂C = 0, S_{φ(i)} ⇀ C.

audit.reason: Good slicing radii produce global integer multiplicity truncations with the claimed local bounds. The diagonal construction gives a current limit; closure gives integrality, and agreement on expanding balls proves both boundary vanishing and the exact currentEval convergence.

Source: Simon 7.2.4 (1)–(11) with Remark 7.2.5(2). Errata: S̃_j = S'_j⌞W_α − P_j (printed +); the printed sets W_γ (γ>α, γ ↓ 0; correct: γ<α) are not needed: we compare on B_{G₃} (step 7). Siblings: (VO) vanish_off_support; (MR) mass_and_support (first conjunct); (IMC)(b)–(d) foundations; (SL) slicing; (BR) closure_and_boundary_rectifiability (second conjunct); (FL) flat_convergence; (PF) pushforward.
Conventions. n:=m+1; IM:=integer multiplicity; B_r:=ball(0,r), B̄_r:=closedBall(0,r); A(ω):=currentEval A ω; X+Y:=X−(0−Y) for currents in one domain (contract Sub; IM by IMC(c), 0 being IM via the empty IMRep); M(X):=X.mass; μ_A:=R_A.measure for an IMRep R_A of an IM A; μ_j:=μ_{S_j}.
(F1) For A IM in an open V: M_G(A) = μ_A(G) for open G (MR); μ_A(ℝ^P∖V)=0 (carrier⊆V); μ_A(K')<∞ for compact K'⊆V (locallyIntegrable_mult); μ_A(V∖spt A)=0, as V∖spt A = V∩zeroRegion(A) is open and A kills the forms admissible for it, whose tsupports miss spt A (VO).
(F2) (Locality.) If A₁, A₂ are IM in open V₁, V₂, O⊆V₁∩V₂ is open and A₁(ω) = A₂(ω) for test ω with tsupport ω⊆O, then μ_{A₁} = μ_{A₂} on Borel subsets of O: μ_{A₁}(G) = M_G(A₁) = M_G(A₂) = μ_{A₂}(G) for open G⊆O (F1; same admissible forms, same values); the open O_q:=B_q∖cthickening(1/q, ℝ^P∖O) (q≥1; O_q=B_q if O=ℝ^P) increase to O and have compact closures in O, so the finite (F1) μ_{A_i}⌞O_q, agreeing on open sets (a π-system generating the Borel sets) and on ℝ^P, coincide; let q→∞ (continuity from below).
(F3) (Subadditivity.) For A, B IM in an open V and Borel E, μ_{A±B}(E)≤μ_A(E)+μ_B(E): for open E by F1 and M_E(A±B)≤M_E(A)+M_E(B) (ofReal((A±B)(ω))≤ofReal(A(ω))+ofReal(±B(ω)) for admissible ω; −ω is admissible); for Borel E⊆O_q (F2, O:=V) by outer regularity of the finite μ_A⌞O_q, μ_B⌞O_q, μ_{A±B}⌞O_q (intersect the open approximants), then q→∞, all three vanishing off V. The same ofReal bound gives M_G(X+Y)≤M_G(X)+M_G(Y) for any currents, G open.
(F4) (Restriction.) For A IM in an open V with IMRep (M_A,θ_A,ξ_A) and E Borel, (M_A∩E,θ_A,ξ_A) is an IMRep in V (IMC(b)) of a current A⌞E, (A⌞E)(ω) = ∫_{M_A∩E}θ_Aξ_A(ω) dHⁿ: A⌞E is IM, μ_{A⌞E} = μ_A⌞E, A⌞E = A on forms vanishing off E, and A⌞E kills forms vanishing on E. If E⊆E'⊆V, E' compact, the triple is also an IMRep in ℝ^P (∫_{M_A∩E∩K'}θ_A≤μ_A(E')<∞ for compact K'; other fields unchanged) of a current in ℝ^P (IMC(b) in ℝ^P, E:=ℝ^P), again A⌞E. (R.measure, R.orient) is a representation as in (SL): R.measure = θ_AHⁿ⌞M_A is finite on compact subsets of V, R.orient is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M_A, hence for R.measure, |R.orient α|≤|α| a.e. (IMC(d)), A(ω) = ∫R.orient(ω) dR.measure; the currents ∫_Eξ(ω)dμ of (SL) are exactly the A⌞E.
(F5) (Domain restriction.) If X is IM in ℝ^P and spt X is a compact subset of an open V, X|_V:=X.restrictDomain (subset_univ V)∈𝒟_n(V) is IM: IMC(b) in ℝ^P (E:=V) gives an IMRep (all fields) with carrier (carrier of X)∩V, a μ_X-null change (F1), so still representing X; its carrier lies in V and its multiplicity is integrable on compact subsets of V, so the same data are an IMRep in V of X|_V. Also ∂(X|_V) = (∂X)|_V, spt X|_V⊆spt X, μ_{X|_V} = μ_X on Borel subsets of V (F2), M_G(X|_V)≤M_G(X) for open G (forms admissible for X|_V are admissible for X).

1. (Reduction to ψ=id.)
